title: Introduce cross-slice quantile-trend fusion canary with entropy gating
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: We observed recurring noisy short-lived latency regressions that pass single-slice detectors but cause user-visible blips under specific traffic blends. This PR introduces a cross-slice quantile-trend fusion detector that combines quantile deltas across stratified traffic slices and uses an entropy-based gate to reduce false positives from low-information slices. The approach fuses short-term and medium-term quantile trends per slice, weights them by traffic fraction and slice stability, and aggregates a probabilistic confidence score. An entropy gate suppresses alerts when per-slice signal entropy is below threshold, preventing overreaction to low-variance or single-outlier dominated slices. Key outcomes: improved precision at 95% recall on historical regressions, reduced false positive rate by ~32% in replay tests, and integration into the rollout guard pipeline as an optional check for staged rollouts. Implementation notes: Added a new fusion runtime component that accepts per-slice histograms, computes trend vectors, and emits a fused quantile delta with confidence metadata. The entropy gate computes normalized slice entropy over a sliding window and sets an adaptive suppression factor. This PR includes deterministic offline replay tests and a lightweight in-cluster canary emulator for smoke testing. Rollout plan: feature flagged behind canary.experimental.cross_slice_quantile_fusion, enabled in canary-runner for internal perf-canary and gradually rolled to production canaries after one week of green metrics and manual signoff. Related work: complements the temporal-cohort consensus detector and the multiscale fingerprint quarantiner; references ENG-2207 for evaluation harness and ENG-2215 for entropy heuristics. Breaking changes: none. Commits summary: feat(fusion): add cross-slice quantile trend fusion engine; feat(gates): add entropy gate and adaptive suppression; test: add unit and replay tests with historical regression fixtures; ci: add integration job and update canary-runner config; docs: runbook and onboarding notes. Changed areas: core fusion algorithm in src/canary/fusion/quantile_fusion.py; entropy gate implementation in src/canary/gates/entropy_gate.py; new cross-slice aggregation API at src/canary/api/aggregation.py; canary-runner wiring in deployments/canary-runner/config.yml; replay harness updates in tools/replay/harness.py; unit and replay tests in tests/canary/; documentation in docs/runbooks/canary-quantile-fusion.md. Testing: local unit tests and deterministic replays on a 30-day window of production traffic including 12 known regressions were used to calibrate thresholds. Integration CI runs include a canary-emulator that simulates slice-level traffic and validated that the fusion detector preserves latency SLOs under injected regressions. Observability: new metrics (fusion.confidence, fusion.fused_delta_q90, fusion.suppress_reason) and dashboards added to perf-canary team Grafana. Backwards compatibility: aggregation API accepts legacy per-slice histogram payloads; when feature flag is off the system falls back to existing single-slice detectors. Merge and deployment: PR merged via squash after approvals, feature behind flag, gradual rollout with telemetry-based gating. Runbook: docs/runbooks/canary-quantile-fusion.md contains remediation steps and guidance for threshold tuning.

review_comments: Luca Perez: Nice design. Can you clarify the complexity of the fusion step at 1k slices? We need an upper bound for scheduling.

Maya Thompson: The fusion step is O(n*logk) where k is quantile bins; added a note and a benchmark in tests to show 1.2ms median on 1k slices on c5.xlarge-equivalent. See tests/canary/bench_fusion.py.
Anya Kline: Entropy gate looks reasonable but we should avoid too aggressive suppression during low traffic windows. Can you add adaptive scaling?
Maya Thompson: Added adaptive scaling that lowers suppression during windows where total throughput < 200 qps; rationale documented in runbook.
Samir Rao: Integration CI flaked once on canary-emulator, reran and passed. Approving.
